data.body:
FINAL rebar-debug REPORT — landed in Gerrit 1556 and mirrored on main at 8c9bf5d78d246f94340c913e6d90a36232cb608d.

Problem: Python 3.11 intermittently hung TestClient teardown after test_matching_guard_is_accepted, so the CI hang guard killed the xdist worker.

Proven root cause: src/rebar/opcert_service/app.py formerly wrapped asyncio.to_thread(jobs.run_job, ...) in asyncio.wait_for. On Python 3.11, CPython issue 86296 allows wait_for to consume an external cancellation when its child completes in the same turn. Runtime traces observed the worker return to queue.get() with cancelling()==1 while lifespan (app.py:55-59) awaited it forever. The intervention replacing only wait_for semantics with asyncio.timeout made the report pass and killed the xdist/TestClient/executor alternatives.

Proof: the deterministic harness produced done=False/cancelled=False/cancelling=1 under Python 3.11 and done=True/cancelled=True under 3.12. The real TestClient trace observed cancellation enter the old wait_for branch and then the worker loop. Baseline reproduced 3/3; the one-line semantic intervention passed 20/20.

RED→GREEN oracle: tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py:199 test_worker_cancellation_survives_job_completion_race was observed RED before production changes, physically held out from the fixer, and GREEN after the fix on Python 3.11 and 3.12. An exact mutation restoring wait_for returned it to RED on 3.11; restoring the fix returned GREEN. Review added tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py:151 test_worker_records_job_timeout so the retained timeout contract is explicit.

Fix: app.py:76-83 now uses async with asyncio.timeout(...) around the same to_thread call. This matches Python 3.12 wait_for semantics, preserves external cancellation, and retains the configured per-job timeout. No queue, ACK, record-schema, or public surface changed.

Scope and safety: _worker has only the lifespan caller; uvicorn/compose and TestClient all use that same app. No caller depends on swallowed cancellation. The fix restores documented bounded queue/shutdown behavior, adds no dependency, weakens no test, and changes no API/wire/config/legacy contract. Existing accepted-job, terminal-record, matching-guard, and timeout behavior remain covered.

Sibling sweeps: construct sweep found no other direct asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.to_thread(...)) lifecycle occurrence. The review-bot indirect timeout path has bounded shutdown cancellation and is not a confirmed sibling. Parity census: CLI/library/MCP are N/A (internal opcert worker lifecycle); the HTTP opcert service and automated container deployment both route through this single lifespan/worker; dual direction is N/A. No MISSING slot remains.

Replication: the original test passed 20/20 single-process and 20/20 under -n 4 --dist worksteal on Python 3.11. The opcert suite passed 21/21 on Python 3.11 and 21/21 on Python 3.12. Held-out cancellation oracle passed both versions; lint/complexity, mypy, module-size, and diff checks passed. Gerrit recorded LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, zero unresolved comments, and merged the fix.

Residual risk/prevention: accepted — lifespan still has no separate bound around awaiting a cancelled worker, but the only evidenced path that defeated cancellation is repaired and the timeout remains bounded; adding a second shutdown policy without a failing mechanism would expand scope. Prevention is the held-out cancellation-race oracle plus explicit timeout-contract regression. No other observed fragility is undispositioned.
